Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the chase. Phoebe Litchfield and Georgia Voll are ready to take on the task, and Marizanne Kapp is geared up to bowl the first over. Australia aims to wrap up the win with ease, needing just 98 runs to get across the line. Let's see how this one plays out!
... The Run Chase ...

The final wicket tally of just a mere 97 runs tells the story of utter domination by the Australian attack, spearheaded by Alana King. For South Africa, it was a day best forgotten, as they failed to build partnerships. The target now sits at a low 98 for the Australians. Now surely, South Africa Women can't snatch a victory from the jaws of defeat, can they? Stay tuned as we will be back with Australia Womens' reply in a short while...

Australian leg-spinner Alana King expressed her satisfaction with her performance. King highlighted the importance of quickly assessing the playing conditions, particularly with the drizzle affecting the ball's movement. She credited her success to her coaches, mentors, and teammates, emphasizing the strong team culture and self-belief within the Australian squad. King also mentioned her willingness to focus on her bowling role and let the batters take charge, showcasing her confidence and contentment with her position in the team.

It was all Alana King from then on. What an exhibition of classical leg-spin bowling! She completely dismantled the South African middle and lower order, ripping through the lineup. South Africa Women lost their wickets cheaply, often for single-digit scores. Sinalo Jafta offered a brief, counter-attacking burst with a fighting 29, but even she couldn't escape the mastery of King, who claimed her seven wickets to finish with exceptional figures. A dream spell for any bowler.

It was the King's Day Out in Indore. It was a tough start for the Proteas as the Australian quicks wasted no time getting amongst the wickets. Schutt and Garth delivered the early blows, sending both South African openers back to the pavilion. While Laura Wolvaardt showed her class with a quick 31 runs, building an early platform, the dismissal of the top order brought the spinners into play, and that is where the narrative of the innings changed completely.

Commentary.Commentary: Done and dusted with the pre-match formalities, and it is now time to get the play underway. The umpires and the players make their way out to the middle. Laura Wolvaardt and Tazmin Brits will open up for the South Africa Women. Megan Schutt has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

We are just a few minutes away from all the action. The two sets of players walk out and line up for their respective national anthems. It will be the national anthem of South Africa Women first, followed by that of Australia Women.

Pitch Report - Carlos Brathwaite and Dinesh Karthik are pitchside. They say that this pitch is similar to the previous game and there could be a bit of turn here and the ball could stay low. Australia's decision to bowl first was right, with dew possibly a factor. The batters should use their feet or try playing the sweep shot.

Laura Wolvaardt, the skipper of South Africa Women, says that she would have bowled too as this is a chasing ground. She adds that she feels good to see contributions from their batting side. Mentions that they have two changes as Sinalo Jafta is back in and Masabata Klaas is in for Nondumiso Shangase. Ends by saying that this is a special day and they will look to finish at the top of the table.

Australia Women, says that they will bowl first. She says that it has been a chasing ground and it gets better to bat under lights. She adds that they are getting closer to a perfect game and she hopes to get some momentum from this game. TOSS - Australia Women have won the toss and will BOWL first.

With the winner earning the prize of a direct meeting with India and the right to carry the momentum of a top-spot finish into the final four, this match is anything but a dead rubber. It's a high-stakes battle for supremacy, a true dress rehearsal for the sharp end of the tournament. So, which side will come out on top? We shall find out together. Toss and team news to follow shortly...

On the other side, Proteas Women showed their batting firepower in a rain-reduced slugfest against Pakistan. Led by Laura Wolvaardt's fluent 90, a Sune Luus half-century, and a late Marizanne Kapp onslaught, they piled on a formidable total before their bowlers decimated the top order in the chase. They are clearly playing with confidence and have a history of causing an upset against the mighty Australians. Their bowling attack will be key in trying to dismantle an Australian lineup that, despite its depth, showed a wobble in their previous game.

Australia, the defending champions, enter this contest having survived a major scare in their last outing against England, turning a disastrous 68 for 4 into a stunning victory thanks to the epic, unbeaten 180-run fifth-wicket partnership between centurion Ashleigh Gardner and the gritty Annabel Sutherland, who fell just shy of her ton. There's a question mark looming over their captain, Alyssa Healy, whose calf strain caused her to miss the last game. The Aussies will be sweating on her fitness, desperate to avoid a repeat of last year's T20 World Cup, where her absence proved costly against these very opponents.

Welcome to the highly-anticipated final league clash of the Women's World Cup, a true 'top-of-the-table' decider! While both Australia and South Africa have already punched their tickets to the semis, the winner of this heavyweight will earn the massive advantage of heading straight to Navi Mumbai to lock horns with the formidable hosts, India, in the second semifinal. The stakes are immense, as top spot isn't just about bragging rights, it's about securing the most favourable route to the final dance.
... MATCH DAY ...

Even though the semi-finalists have been decided, this match between Australia Women and South Africa Women still packs a punch. Australia's goal will be to secure the top spot in the table with a win, while South Africa aims to climb up the table. The match between Australia Women and South Africa Women is set to take place at the Holkar Stadium in Indore. Australia Women, who have been in top form throughout the tournament, will be relying on their strong batting lineup, featuring Ellyse Perry, Phoebe Litchfield, and Beth Mooney, as well as their all-rounders, including Tahlia McGrath, Annabel Sutherland, and Ashleigh Gardner, who bring balance to the team with their batting and bowling. The Australian bowling attack, led by Megan Schutt, Alana King, and Darcie Brown, will look to restrict South Africa's scoring opportunities, while wicketkeeper-skipper Alyssa Healy's availability is uncertain due to a minor calf strain, although it's unlikely they'll risk their skipper given their semi-final spot is already secured. Meanwhile, South Africa Women, led by Laura Wolvaardt, will be looking to cause an upset against the Australians, with their top-order batters Tazmin Brits and the skipper herself aiming to provide a solid start, while all-rounders Chloe Tryon, Nadine de Klerk, and Marizanne Kapp provide depth in both batting and bowling. South Africa Women will be looking to exploit the weakness of the Aussie batting unit, which has struggled at times. The winner of this top-of-the-table clash will finish the round stage in first position and head to Mumbai to meet India in the semi-finals, while the loser will face England in the other semi-final in Guwahati, making this match a crucial one for both teams as they look to make a strong impression ahead of the knockout stages.
